intro: Ten stories from the last day, rewritten in plain British English. Tap any word you don't know.

items.title: Protests sweep across Europe
items.text: Protesters took to the streets in France, Italy, Spain, Portugal and Albania on Saturday. They were angry about pensions, housing, living costs, corruption and war. In France, about 2,400 people have been arrested, and nearly 1,000 members of the security forces have been injured. In Tirana, the capital of Albania, police fired tear gas after clashes broke out and government buildings were attacked. Italian police briefly detained 371 people in eight cities, including 110 minors.

gloss.break out: to start suddenly (used for fights, fires and wars)
gloss.tear gas: a gas that makes eyes burn, used by police to disperse crowds
gloss.detain: to hold someone for a short time without charging them
gloss.living costs: the money people need to pay for housing, food and bills
gloss.minor: a person under the age of 18

items.title: Rubio urges Cubans to work with the CIA
items.text: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio has called on Cubans who want change to form what he described as a discreet partnership with the CIA. The Trump administration wants to change the leadership of Cuba. President Trump has said the country is ready to fall. The comments have increased tension between Washington and Havana. Cuban officials have not yet been quoted in the report that Euronews published on Saturday.

gloss.call on: to ask or urge someone to do something
gloss.partnership: a relationship in which two sides work together
gloss.leadership: the people who are in charge of a country or group
gloss.administration: the government of a country, especially the US
gloss.tension: a feeling of worry and anger between two sides

items.title: Healey to deliver his first Budget on Wednesday
items.text: Chancellor John Healey will present the Autumn Budget on Wednesday 28 October. It is his first Budget since he took over the job. Reports say he may change the rules on capital gains tax and give more money to social care. Other ideas include a rise in the business rates threshold and a higher tax on banks. None of these measures has been confirmed yet. Full details of the Your First Home scheme are also due on the day.

gloss.take over: to begin to do a job that someone else did before
gloss.capital gains tax: a tax on the profit you make when you sell something valuable
gloss.social care: help with daily life for older or disabled people
gloss.threshold: the level at which a rule or tax starts to apply
gloss.confirm: to say officially that something is true

items.title: Spurs win at Chelsea as Palmer is sent off
items.text: Tottenham won 2-0 at Stamford Bridge on Saturday. Chelsea goalkeeper Mike Penders punched a corner into his own net in the second half. Mathys Tel then scored a solo goal with about ten minutes left. Cole Palmer was sent off for a second yellow card. Spurs had won only one of their previous 34 Premier League visits to Chelsea. It was also their first clean sheet at the ground in all competitions since December 1986.

gloss.send off: to order a player to leave the pitch for a serious foul
gloss.own goal: a goal scored by mistake against your own team
gloss.clean sheet: a match in which a team does not let in a goal
gloss.yellow card: a warning shown to a player by the referee

items.title: Villa end Manchester City's perfect start
items.text: Aston Villa beat Manchester City 2-1 at Villa Park on Saturday. The result ended City's perfect start to the Premier League season. Villa's Jackson scored, and City's Erling Haaland also found the net. City had won all of their league games before the match. The game opened Matchweek 8 and kicked off at 12.30pm in Birmingham. Villa therefore beat the league leaders at home.

gloss.perfect start: a start with no defeats or dropped points
gloss.league leaders: the team at the top of the table
gloss.matchweek: one round of games in a league season

items.title: Electric flights 'only ten years away'
items.text: A Dutch researcher says passengers in Europe could book an electric flight within ten years. Maarten Steinbuch believes aircraft makers should move to electric power, as car companies have done. A Dutch start-up called Elysian Aircraft is building a battery-powered passenger plane. He says the change would follow the path that the car industry has already taken.

gloss.start-up: a new company, often one that builds new technology
gloss.battery-powered: working with electricity stored in a battery
gloss.exhaust fumes: the gases an engine sends out into the air
gloss.move to: to change to a different system or method
gloss.route: the path a plane or vehicle takes between two places

items.title: Why standard time may be better for health
items.text: The clocks go back in the UK and much of Europe this weekend. Experts say that permanent standard time would be healthier than switching clocks twice a year. Changing the time can upset sleep and the body clock, which controls when people feel tired or awake. The clocks change again in spring. Euronews looked at what the research says about winter time and summer time.

gloss.standard time: the normal local time without the summer change
gloss.switch: to change from one thing to another
gloss.upset: to disturb or make something worse
gloss.body clock: the natural system that controls when you sleep and wake

items.title: Gen Z wants better stories on screen
items.text: A 2026 report on teens and screens says young viewers want better representation in the stories they watch. They like YouTube and are less opposed to artificial intelligence in storytelling than many adults expected. Neurodivergent representation is also an important topic in the report. The findings suggest that Gen Z and Gen Alpha are changing how film, television and online video are made. Euronews reported the findings on Saturday.

gloss.representation: showing different kinds of people fairly in the media
gloss.neurodivergent: having a brain that works differently from what is typical, for example autism or ADHD
gloss.audience: the people who watch or listen to something

items.title: Moody's spares France a downgrade
items.text: The rating agency Moody's has kept France's sovereign credit rating unchanged, although many people expected a downgrade. Economists say the decision is only a brief respite, not a vote of confidence. France still faces high public debt. Protests and unrest have also hit the country this month. A lower rating would normally make it more expensive for a government to borrow money. Moody's decision was reported on Saturday.

gloss.respite: a short break from something difficult
gloss.vote of confidence: a sign that people trust someone or something
gloss.public debt: the total money a government owes
gloss.unrest: anger and disorder among a large group of people

items.title: GTA VI pre-orders pass six million
items.text: Grand Theft Auto VI has reached an estimated 6.45 million pre-orders, according to the research firm Sensor Tower. That is worth about 630 million dollars. Around 74 per cent of the orders are for PlayStation 5. Rockstar Games will release the game on 19 November on PS5 and Xbox Series consoles. The standard edition costs 79.99 dollars, and an earlier forecast said sales could pass 45 million copies at launch.

gloss.pre-order: to pay for a product before it is released
gloss.estimate: a rough calculation of a number
gloss.edition: a particular version of a product
gloss.forecast: a statement about what will probably happen
gloss.launch: the time when a product first goes on sale
